Build a balanced ternary lattice code by greedy lexicographic selection plus top-50 swap improvement, then break symmetry with annealed soft-max repulsion with and without lattice anchoring and LP-polish, keeping the best vs the record.
direction: Search a structured algebraic basin via a quantised lattice code followed by symmetry-breaking continuous relaxation. Enumerate all normalised vectors in $\{-1,0,1\}^{13}$ with support size 3 or 4 (about 13,700 candidates, whose pairwise cosines are multiples of $1/3$ or $1/4$), then greedily build a 95-subset minimising the lexicographic pair profile: at each step choose the candidate minimising (maximum dot to the chosen set, number of pairs attaining it, $\sum\exp(20\cdot\mathrm{dot})$). Improve the discrete set with replacement swaps—try swapping each selected point against the 200 best unused candidates and accept any swap that lexicographically lowers the sorted list of the top 50 pair cosines—for ~30s. Then release the lattice constraint: smooth-relax with $\beta=30\to500$, LP-polish, and additionally keep a symmetry-penalised variant for the first half of relaxation (penalty on distance to the nearest lattice point, weight decaying to zero) so the continuous optimum inherits the lattice topology rather than sliding back to the record basin; compare against `best.npy` and return the better.

idea: Escape the jammed record with soft-mode kicks from the contact rigidity matrix and coherent cluster rotations, screened by short LP polish.
direction: Generate kicks along the soft modes of the contact rigidity matrix and as coherent contact-cluster rotations, not isotropic noise. Build the active pair set with cosine $>$ max$-0.005$ (cap at the top 1500), assemble the sparse tangent Jacobian $J$ whose row for pair $(i,j)$ is $x_j$ in block $i$ plus $x_i$ in block $j$ projected orthogonal to $x_i,x_j$, and compute its smallest ~25 right singular vectors with `scipy.sparse.linalg.svds`. Trial displacements are $x+\alpha v$ for those vectors with $\alpha\in\{0.02,0.05,0.1,0.2\}$ (projected tangent and renormalised), screened by a 0.5s LP polish; in parallel, trial cluster moves that pick an overloaded centre, take its 10–25 contact neighbours, and rotate that whole cluster by angles $0.05$–$0.25$ in a random tangent 2-plane while leaving the rest fixed. Long-polish only screened trials that either beat the record or reach within $10^{-4}$ of it with a contact adjacency (threshold max$-10^{-3}$) differing from the record's, since a near-tie with a new topology is valuable.

idea: Escape the jammed vertex with coordinated cap re-jamming: large clustered perturbations re-optimized by smooth-max annealing to change contact topology before short LP screening.
Batched fresh-start population search with annealed soft-max Adam and fingerprint-pruned crossover.
direction: Run a batched fresh-start population search that never seeds from the record except as final fallback, to discover genuinely different basins. Maintain $B=24$ configurations of shape $(24,95,13)$ (random Gaussian rows plus low-discrepancy sphere points), and optimise all simultaneously with batched Adam on the annealed soft maximum $E_\beta=\beta^{-1}\log\sum_{i<j}\exp(\beta\langle x_i,x_j\rangle)$, with $\beta=20\to80\to250\to700$, step size $0.01$ decaying to $0.002$, tangent-projected gradients via batched Gram matrices, for roughly 60–80s. Every 10s record each member's true maximum, prune duplicates using a permutation-invariant fingerprint (sorted Gram eigenvalues plus the sorted contact-count vector at max$-0.002$), and apply crossover to the survivors by transplanting the 15–25 lowest-contact points of one elite into the voids of another. LP-polish the top three mutually distinct elites for ~15s each, then long-polish the winner; return it only if it beats `best.npy`.

Delete a large hub-centred contact patch and rebuild it hole-by-hole with frozen-core annealed repulsion before unfreezing.
direction: Delete and rebuild a large contact-graph patch: remove the rattler, all points with fewer than 8 contacts, and a connected cluster around a maximum-contact hub such as point 44, for 15-22 removed points total, because deleting only 1-5 points leaves the old topology intact. Reinsert the removed points one at a time into the largest spherical holes of the current configuration, found from at least 20,000 random candidates followed by local minimisation of the maximum dot product, then jointly refine only the inserted points with annealed softmax repulsion ($\beta=50\to800$) against the frozen core before unfreezing everything for a short LP polish; repeat with different hub-centred clusters and seeds under strict time-boxing, returning the best configuration encountered.

idea: Dual-stress contact surgery that deactivates low-marginal contacts and re-optimizes them toward tighter targets before full LP polish.
direction: Perform dual-stress contact surgery rather than random shaking: run one LP polish, extract the LP inequality marginals for all pairs with slack $<10^{-9}$, rank contacts by absolute dual stress, and repeatedly choose 10-30 low-stress contacts involving 8-20 points to deliberately deactivate. With the remaining points initially frozen, solve a feasibility problem for the chosen points with target cosines stepping through $0.2438, 0.2433, 0.2425$, using Adam or SLSQP on $\sum \mathrm{softplus}((\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-t)/10^{-4})$ over active plus deactivated pairs, then unfreeze all points, LP-polish, and keep the result only if it beats $0.244097856927$; enforce an internal 150-second deadline and always fall back to the record.

idea: Cyclic C13 orbit construction with 7 full orbits plus 4 free/partial-orbit points optimized by annealed log-sum-exp Adam then symmetry-broken full refinement and LP squeeze.
direction: Search a symmetry-constrained orbit construction from scratch to obtain balanced contacts by design: use the cyclic group $C_{13}$ acting by cyclic coordinate shifts, parametrise 7 free representatives in $\mathbb{R}^{13}$ to generate $7\times13=91$ points, add 4 freely optimised points to reach 95, and optimise all representatives with Adam on a log-sum-exp approximation to the maximum pairwise cosine, annealing $\beta$ from 30 to 1000 and penalising coincident orbit points. After optimisation, break the symmetry with a tiny tangent perturbation ($10^{-3}$-$10^{-2}$), LP-polish, and compare against the record; also try replacing the 4 free points by a second partially constrained orbit family if duplicates or excessive internal cosines appear.

Search cyclic-shift symmetric basins via global Fourier power spectrum plus random phases with DE/random search, break symmetry with tangent noise and annealed softmax Adam, then LP-polish the best.
direction: Search a genuinely different symmetric basin using a cyclic-orbit construction in the prime dimension 13: generate candidate vectors as orbits under cyclic coordinate shifts of a few real seed vectors, equivalently parameterised by Fourier amplitudes on frequencies $1,\ldots,6$, choose orbit sizes and multiplicities summing to 95, and optimise only the low-dimensional seed parameters with `scipy.optimize.differential_evolution` or random search against the exact maximum cosine for at most 60 seconds. Take the best two or three symmetric codes, add tangent Gaussian symmetry-breaking noise of sizes 0.01, 0.03 and 0.08, refine each with annealed softmax Adam ($\beta:30\to500$, no LP during screening), and LP-polish only the best refined result for the final 25 seconds, returning the better of it and the loaded record.

idea: Delete rattler/hub to 94 points, softmax-polish, insert refined largest-hole vector, relax, tabu-cycle then final LP squeeze.
direction: Use a 94-to-95 bridge to exploit the rattler: delete the rattler from the record and LP/softmax-polish the remaining 94 points, which should gain appreciable slack; then locate the largest empty cap by sampling 50,000 unit vectors, refining the best 20 by minimising their maximum dot product to the 94 points, inserting the best hole vector as the new 95th point, and relaxing all 95 points. Repeat this delete-a-different-point/reinsert-in-largest-hole cycle, on later iterations deleting a high-contact hub rather than the newly inserted point and keeping a tabu list to avoid cycling, for at most 140 seconds; retain every distinct 95-point result, rank them by maximum cosine, and spend only the last 30 seconds LP-polishing the best one.

idea: Cooperative rattler-plus-hub clique surgery with frozen-hole reinsertion via 30k search plus beta-200 tangent Adam and short annealed softmax screening, saving LP for one final polish.
direction: Perform cooperative rattler-plus-hub surgery: from `best.npy`, compute contacts at tolerance $10^{-7}$, remove the rattler together with sets of 4–8 points chosen from the highest-contact hubs that are mutually in contact, freeze the remaining points, and reinsert the removed points one at a time into the largest spherical holes found from 30,000 random candidates followed by 300 steps of tangent Adam minimising a $\beta=200$ softmax of their dot products against the frozen points. After all removed points are placed, run annealed softmax relaxation on all points for at most 5 seconds and accept the trial only if its unpolished maximum is below 0.26; cycle through different hub/rattler subsets with different seeds until 150 seconds, then give the best accepted trial one final 20-second LP polish, with a hard return of the incumbent before 175 seconds.

idea: Basin-hop with cheap annealed soft-max Adam repulsion to screen large shakes and joint worst-point hole re-insertions, reserving trust-region LP for one final squeeze.
Regularised continuation with annealed softmax minimax plus frame and row-max variance penalties optimised by tangent-space Adam from three perturbed records, then one LP polish.
direction: Break the degenerate tie structure with a regularised continuation method and no LP until the end: starting from copies of the record perturbed by tangent noise of sizes 0.03, 0.08 and 0.15, minimise with tangent-space Adam the objective $\mathrm{logsumexp}(\beta G)/\beta+\lambda\lVert X^{T}X-(95/13)I\rVert_F^2+\mu\,\mathrm{Var}_i(\max_{j\ne i}G_{ij})$, annealing $\beta$ from 25 to 600 while decaying $\lambda$ from $10^{-2}$ to $0$ and $\mu$ from $10^{-3}$ to $0$ over at most 2,000 vectorised steps per copy. This explicitly penalises frame anisotropy and unequal per-point maxima while gradually restoring the true minimax objective; check wall time every 50 steps, stop all exploration by 145 seconds, run a single trust-region LP polish on the best copy for the remaining time, and return the incumbent unchanged if that polish does not improve it.
